note: Every release of the engine, newest first, said once as data: its version, its date, a title and a sentence, and a picture of it working. A client that tells people about the product - the company's changelog page - reads this from the release it pins, so the page lists every release and cannot list one that was never cut. CHANGELOG.md is the long account of each release; tests/test_releases.py holds its headings to the versions and dates here, every feature's `since` (features.json) to a release here, and the newest release to the version pyproject.toml states. `shows` is what the release printed when it was run: `run` is typed in a fresh git repository named fernhollow (shown as ~/fernhollow), holding `files` if any, or a copy of the fixture company if `fixture` is true; `output` is what it printed, in order, with a line of just … where lines are left out. The test runs the newest release's again, on every change, so the picture of the current release cannot drift from what it does; an older one's is history, true of the release that printed it.

releases.title: Tell us
releases.says: A developer tells their agent to ping us, and this is what the agent runs: wherefore report writes a bug, a question or a feature request for the engine's makers - the release, the corpus's shape, the output given, the person's words, nothing private - and opens it as an issue, or shows it first.

releases.title: The map says what it is
releases.says: What nobody regenerates is written, not built - by a person or by an agent - and the map says so, never 'by hand'. wherefore graph --home puts a way back to the site on it, and a theme gets two marks beside the accent, so a brand whose accent is a highlighter writes with its ink and marks with the accent.

releases.title: The notice reads nothing new
releases.says: The gate's palette notice counts colours only in the files the build made - which the gate wrote and compared anyway - so a courtesy never widens what the gate opens. The first client records every file its gate reads; 0.10.0 had broken that promise.

import pathlib
pathlib.Path('site').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pathlib.Path('site/a.css').write_text('a { color: #17181B; }\n')
pathlib.Path('site/b.css').write_text('b { color: #F7F6F2; }\n')

releases.title: One palette
releases.says: A brand is a fact like a price. wherefore check palette reads every tracked text file and fails a colour that is not one the brand's source holds, unless the file says, with why, whose colours they are. On by default: the gate says when colours are said in several files and no palette is declared.

releases.says: wherefore graph --theme CSS puts a corpus's own stylesheet where the page's light and dark palettes were, so the map reads the brand's custom properties and carries no second palette typed into the engine.

releases.title: The map credits itself
releases.says: A corpus may publish its own map: a run generator that is wherefore graph, so the page is built and judged like any other file. Under the gate it runs; under wherefore graph it is credited with the files it names rather than run, so the map never maps itself without end.

releases.title: What builds what
releases.says: wherefore graph runs every generator once, traces what each reads and writes, and draws the chain as one self-contained page: every source, the scripts that read it, and everything they make. Choose a source to see what changes with it. It classifies every file as the gate does, and puts the tree back as it found it.

releases.title: A generator can be any command
releases.says: A generator can be any program - node, a shell script, a CAD export - declared by run, its command as a list of words, with no Python wrapper. What it writes is seen by comparing the tree before and after it runs, on the ctime no process can set back, so it is held exactly as strictly as a Python generator.

Start your %s day free trial.

\n" "$(cat ../facts.txt)" > ../site/index.html

releases.title: Every surface, held to the source
releases.says: The skill now asks where else the product is described and sets each surface up to pin the source and fail its build on a feature it does not say. A copy taken from somewhere that cannot be pinned - another site, another product - says where it came from, and wherefore check upstream fails when that source moves. Every release is said once, as data, so a changelog is built rather than kept.

releases.title: Scan: the first win, with no setup
releases.says: Point wherefore scan at a built site, a docs folder or a live address, and it reports every value stated more than one way. It needs no configuration, and it would rather miss a disagreement than invent one.
